rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable B2B role — the ops lead or founder of a small web agency managing 50–200+ client sites on retainer — and they demonstrably already pay for tools like Monday.com, confirming willingness to pay. However, this is a structured SaaS product (per-site records, CMS metadata, renewal tracking, task history) that cannot be shipped as a Claude prompt + form + Stripe link in a week; it requires real data modelling, a persistent multi-tenant database, and a usable UI, which puts buildability at 4 and operational autonomy at 4 — both well below the build gates. The single signal is also weak (one forum post), so volume and reachability need validation before any build commitment.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be a lightweight agency client-site tracker: a simple dashboard where an agency can log each client website (CMS type, renewal date, retainer status, last-task notes) and see everything at a glance. To build it without coding, the factory would need to stand up a real persistent web app with a database — this goes beyond Claude prompts and a Stripe link; it would require a no-code/low-code platform (e.g. Airtable or Notion as the data layer, with a custom view) plus an intake form and a Stripe subscription link for billing. To sell, the factory would identify agency owners on LinkedIn or in agency-focused Slack communities (e.g. Cloudways Agency Partner groups, WP Builds Slack) and draft cold outreach — Youval approves each batch before it sends. Delivery would be self-serve: the agency signs up, gets a Notion/Airtable template pre-populated with their site count, and billing runs via Stripe automatically. The only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and occasional template customisation requests — but a key honest caveat: if agencies want a true standalone SaaS with their own login, custom fields, and integrations, a solo non-technical operator cannot build that without a developer; the Notion/Airtable wrapper is a valid MVP but will hit a ceiling quickly.
notes: Fails two build gates: buildability_with_ai (4, below floor of 6) and operational_autonomy (4, below floor of 7). A true multi-tenant SaaS with per-site data models cannot be shipped as pure Claude + prompts. A no-code MVP is feasible but limited. Validate demand and willingness to pay with a waitlist or concierge pilot before committing to build. Single weak signal — seek 5–10 corroborating conversations.
